title: Decision: the agent serves a JMAP WebSocket, which is how a call signal reaches a client
description:
Mark decided 2026-11-23, for bead mimid-1wgh.114.8.

THE QUESTION. VTCCall/signal sends a session description or candidate
(commit b29cd913). Nothing carries one back. The agent's only push
channel is GET /jmap/eventsource, which carries RFC 8620 §7.3
StateChange objects -- "these types changed, go look" -- and a signal is
not stored, so there is nothing to look at. A client can offer a call,
send its SDP, and wait forever.

CHOSEN: the agent serves a JMAP WebSocket (RFC 8887).

WHY:
- It is what draft-atwood-jmap-vtc-00 assumes: VTCCallSignal is
  specified as an ephemeral WebSocket event, and
  JMAP_VTC_WEBSOCKET_URI is already defined in jmap-vtc-types.
- crate-jmap-websocket already exists in the workspace, so the server
  side is mostly the crate's rather than ours.
- It is two-way, which a client holding a call wants anyway: it sends
  trickled candidates as fast as it receives them, and an HTTP round
  trip each way is the wrong shape for that.
- ParlorVTC's client is built on exactly this shape -- a WebSocket
  subscription per relay, re-subscribed on reconnect -- so a demo client
  (bead mimid-1wgh.114.9) lifts a known design rather than inventing
  one.

NOT CHOSEN:
- Carrying the signal on the existing EventSource. Cheapest by far, and
  the stream is already authenticated, but it puts an event that is not
  a StateChange into RFC 8620's event stream. That is a change to how
  the stream works and would have to be written into the draft rather
  than done quietly, and the next implementer would be surprised by it.
- Storing signals and polling. Contradicts their being ephemeral
  (decision mimid-1wgh.117: signalling is not content), puts SDP in the
  agent's database for nobody's benefit, and adds latency to the one
  part of a call that cannot afford it.

WHAT IT COSTS: a WebSocket upgrade path on the agent's loopback
endpoint, authentication on the socket, and the connection lifecycle
around it. The agent already authenticates a bearer credential on that
endpoint (docs/design/frontend-auth.md §3) and already serves the live
stream's WebSocket to its PROVIDER (mimid-live), so neither the
dependency nor the pattern is new to the crate -- but this is a socket
in the other direction, serving the user's client, and its auth is the
agent's credential table rather than a provider token.

WHAT STAYS TRUE: a signal is still never stored, still not replayed to
a client that was not connected, and still not a record to fetch. The
WebSocket is how it is delivered, not a place it lives.
close_reason: Mark 2026-11-23: the agent serves a JMAP WebSocket; it is what the draft assumes, crate-jmap-websocket already exists, and it is two-way as a calling client needs.
